statements:
statement_A
  (P Q : MeasureTheory.Measure S)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
  (p q : T)
  (hP : R₁ P p)
  (hQ : R₁ Q q)
  (hs : R₂ P p q)
  (hp :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (h : H n),
      (∀ (b : Bool), 0 ≤ p n h b) ∧ ∑ b, p n h b = 1)
  (hq :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (h : H n),
      (∀ (b : Bool), 0 ≤ q n h b) ∧ ∑ b, q n h b = 1)
  (B : ℝ)
  (hB :
    ∀ (n : ℕ),
      ∀ᵐ (x : S) ∂P,
        ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, E P p q k x ≤ B)
  (τ : S → WithTop ℕ)
  (hτ : MeasureTheory.IsStoppingTime F τ)
  (hτP : ∀ᵐ (x : S) ∂P, τ x ≠ ⊤)
  (W : S → ENNReal) (hW : Measurable W)
  (hW2 : ∫⁻ (x : S), W x ^ 2 ∂P < ⊤) :
  ∃ L,
    MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable L ∧
      0 ≤ᵐ[P] L ∧
        MeasureTheory.MemLp L 2 P ∧
          (∀ᵐ (x : S) ∂P,
              Filter.Tendsto (fun n => D P Q n x)
                Filter.atTop (nhds (L x))) ∧
            ∫ (x : S), L x ^ 2 ∂P ≤ Real.exp B ∧
              ∫ (x : S), L x ∂P = 1 ∧
                (Q = P.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (L x)) ∧
                  Q.AbsolutelyContinuous P ∧
                    MeasurableSet {x | τ x ≠ ⊤} ∧
                      (∀ᵐ (x : S) ∂Q, τ x ≠ ⊤) ∧
                        ∫⁻ (x : S), W x ∂P < ⊤ ∧
                          ∫⁻ (x : S), W x ∂Q < ⊤ ∧
                            |(∫⁻ (x : S), W x ∂Q).toReal -
                                  (∫⁻ (x : S),
                                      W x ∂P).toReal| ≤
                              √((Real.exp B - 1) * ProbabilityTheory.variance (fun x => (W x).toReal) P)

statement_B (m : ℝ)
  (hm : 2 ≤ m) :
  have p := (m ^ 2)⁻¹;
  have q := m⁻¹;
  have pt := U p p;
  have qt := U q 1;
  ∃ P Q,
    MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P ∧
      MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure Q ∧
        R₁ P pt ∧
          R₁ Q qt ∧
            R₂ P pt qt ∧
              (∀ (n : ℕ) (h : H n),
                  (∀ (b : Bool), 0 ≤ pt n h b) ∧ ∑ b, pt n h b = 1) ∧
                (∀ (n : ℕ) (h : H n),
                    (∀ (b : Bool), 0 ≤ qt n h b) ∧ ∑ b, qt n h b = 1) ∧
                  (MeasureTheory.IsStoppingTime
                      F fun x => 2) ∧
                    (∀ᵐ (x : S) ∂P, ∀ k ≥ 2, x k = false) ∧
                      (∀ᵐ (x : S) ∂Q,
                          ∀ k ≥ 2, x k = false) ∧
                        (∀ (n : ℕ),
                            ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n,
                                ∫ (x : S),
                                  E P pt qt k
                                    x ∂P <
                              2) ∧
                          Measurable (C m) ∧
                            ∫⁻ (x : S),
                                  C m x ^ 2 ∂P =
                                1 ∧
                              ∫⁻ (x : S),
                                  C m x ∂Q =
                                ENNReal.ofReal m
definition_context: S is ℕ → Bool with the product measurable space, Bool has the discrete measurable space. H n is Fin n → Bool, and T is (n : ℕ) → H n → Bool → ℝ. The prefix at n reads coordinates 0 through n−1, so the prefix at 0 is empty. F n is the σ-algebra pulled back by that prefix map.

Write a(M,n,h) for Measure.real of the event that the length-n prefix equals h under M. R₁ M t means a(M,n+1,snoc(h,b)) = a(M,n,h) * t n h b for every n,h,b. R₂ P p q means at every history with a(P,n,h)>0, p n h b=0 implies q n h b=0.

For the observed prefix h, D P Q n x is a(Q,n,h)/a(P,n,h), using Lean's real division by zero equals zero. E P p q n x is zero if a(P,n,h)=0, otherwise ∑ over b∈Bool of (q n h b−p n h b)²/p n h b, with the same real division convention.

U u v is a table: the probability assigned to true is u at depth zero; at depth one it is v when the first bit is true and zero otherwise; at depths at least two it is zero. The probability assigned to false is one minus the probability assigned to true.
C m x is ENNReal.ofReal of m² if the first two bits are both true, and zero otherwise. It is a terminal charge, not a count of observations.

Q.AbsolutelyContinuous P means every P-null set is Q-null. ∫⁻ is the nonnegative extended Lebesgue integral; .toReal maps ⊤ to zero, so notice which conclusions first prove finiteness. ProbabilityTheory.variance is the variance of the real observable under the displayed measure.
